42 days until the NFL season. Today we’re honoring one of the all-time greats: #42 Paul Warfield.

Paul Warfield came to the Dolphins in 1970 via a blockbuster trade with the Browns and instantly elevated Miami’s offense to championship caliber. Warfield was the kind of receiver who made it all look effortless.

Warfield averaged an incredible 21.5 yards per catch during his time in Miami and was a crucial part of the team’s three straight Super Bowl appearances, including the Perfect Season in 1972.

He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1983 and remains one of the more efficient and dangerous wide receivers in NFL history.

Toney caught 81 passes for 951 yards on first and second down. On third and fourth, he converted 28 catches into 260 yards, four touchdowns and 18 first downs.

Then there is WHERE he caught the ball.

Fifty-four of his 109 receptions came on screens. Those plays produced 446 yards, the second-highest screen total PFF has charted since 2014. His average target depth from the slot was only 6.8 yards.

Toney still finished with:

1,211 receiving yards
841 yards after the catch
285 yards after contact
33 missed tackles forced
58 receiving first downs
24 gains of at least 15 yards
8 gains of at least 25 yards

Nearly 70 percent of his receiving yardage came after the ball arrived. 

Toney repeatedly turned an ordinary throw near the line of scrimmage into a productive play. Miami built huge sections of the offense around that ability.
